title: P2MFDS: A Privacy-Preserving Multimodal Fall Detection System for Elderly People in Bathroom Environments
abstract: arXiv:2506.17332v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: By 2050, people aged 65 and over are projected to make up 16% of the global population. As aging is closely associated with increased fall risk, particularly in wet and confined environments such as bathrooms where over 80% of falls occur. Although recent research has increasingly focused on non-intrusive, privacy-preserving approaches that do not rely on wearable devices or video-based monitoring, these efforts have not fully overcome the limitations of existing unimodal systems (e.g., WiFi-, infrared-, or mmWave-based), which are prone to reduced accuracy in complex environments. These limitations stem from fundamental constraints in unimodal sensing, including system bias and environmental interference, such as multipath fading in WiFi-based systems and drastic temperature changes in infrared-based methods. translated_title: P2MFDS：面向浴室环境中老年人的隐私保护多模态跌倒检测系统
translated_abstract: 到2050年，预计65岁及以上人口将占全球人口的16%。由于衰老与跌倒风险增加密切相关，尤其是在潮湿且封闭的环境中（如浴室），超过80%的跌倒发生于此。尽管近期研究日益关注非侵入性、隐私保护的方法，这些方法不依赖可穿戴设备或基于视频的监控，但仍未能完全克服现有单模态系统（如基于WiFi、红外或毫米波的系统）的局限性，这些系统在复杂环境中易出现精度下降。这些局限性源于单模态传感的基本约束，包括系统偏差和环境干扰，例如基于WiFi系统中的多径衰落以及基于红外方法中的剧烈温度变化。为应对这些挑战，我们提出了一种面向浴室环境中老年人的隐私保护多模态跌倒检测系统。
tldr: 本文提出一种隐私保护的多模态跌倒检测系统，通过融合WiFi、红外和毫米波传感数据，有效克服单模态系统在浴室复杂环境中的精度下降问题，兼顾隐私与可靠性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a privacy-preserving multimodal fall detection system that integrates WiFi, infrared, and mmWave sensing data to overcome accuracy degradation of unimodal systems in complex bathroom environments, balancing privacy and reliability.
